FL-202.label: The model browser: every model the token source offers, ranked, pinnable, with price and context window; the thinking level beside it; the standard configurations one click away.
FL-202.walk: Open the model chip on a conversation: the source's models are listed ranked with price and context window; pin one and it stays on top; pick another and the thread switches to it and stays on it — new conversations start on it too, until you change it, and the chip says so; set the thinking level beside it; pick a standard configuration (pinned, max, elbow, floor) and see what it selects now; switching back from a model to a policy is one click. Ban the model the strategy picked. The next new conversation starts on the next best eligible model, the first keeps its model, and the banned model cannot be pinned. Lift the ban. Check the strategy, ban reason and dated saved pick at phone and desktop width.
FL-202.observed: Verified search, pin to top, floor, budget, elbow, add/lift on desktop and phone, both pin refusals, two actual receipts and thread stickiness. The complete older gesture of changing thinking and inspecting its next request was not repeated.

FL-152.label: Cost routing: lowest cost above an intelligence threshold, or a spend rate per hour buying the most intelligence that burn allows.
FL-152.walk: Set Floor with an intelligence threshold in the token-cost policy; a new thread's chosen model is the cheapest one at or above that threshold. Set Budget with dollars per hour; a new thread's chosen model is the most intelligent one the agents' measured hourly token burn can buy for that, and the readout says what it costs an hour and what the next smarter model would cost.
FL-152.observed: On the installed pair, selected Floor 36, then Budget from the rail after a priced turn. Read each new conversation model and its policy. The budget readout priced the pick and the next smarter model from measured burn. See after/role-and-policy-controls.json.

FL-153.label: The elbow: a standard point on the cost-to-intelligence Pareto curve.
FL-153.walk: Choose the elbow policy; a new thread's policy readout names which frontier model is the elbow, how far below the frontier's price chord it sits, and what the next model up adds for its price. Start an unset home. Its first conversation uses the elbow. With the catalog unreachable, start on its dated eligible saved pick. Repeat in a home that has never read the catalog and verify the refusal starts no turn.
FL-153.observed: Fresh and upgraded conversations paid Muse Ember. The detailed readout named the 0.420 offset, next model and marginal cost. A model ban moved the next conversation to Haiku. The saved pick started a conversation with the catalog endpoint disconnected. A cold home returned model_unavailable before run.started.

FL-206.label: Strategies and models: the strategies rail beside the model list, each strategy with its one-sentence meaning and the model it picks now; one plain summary of the model in use; the strategy named wherever the model is.
FL-206.walk: Open the Model Device from the conversation's model chip: the strategies (Pinned, Max, Elbow, Floor, Budget once the ledger has a burn, Local when offline) stand beside the ranked model list, each with what it means and the model it picks now, the one in force marked; the model in use has one paragraph naming its price in and out (the price the chip quotes), context, rank, thinking level, which strategy chose it and why, and since when. Click Elbow; a new thread's header chip, thread-list row, conversation configuration legend and spend-module model row all read 'Elbow · <model>'. Pick Floor and Budget from the rail the same way.
FL-206.observed: Opened both devices and headers, expanded the price/score/context summary, and changed Floor, Budget and Elbow. The conversation and priced receipt agreed. The full four-surface legend comparison in the Spend module and thread list was not repeated.
